cases.title: Convening global, regional and virtual multi-stakeholder events
cases.initiative: by the 4per1000 Initiative - Soils for Food Security and Climate
cases.contribution: This action is reported as contributing to Objective 8. Land restoration and sustainable agriculture, and Objective 9. More resilient, adaptive, sustainable, and circular food systems.
body: The “4 per 1000” Initiative convenes global, regional, thematic and virtual multi-stakeholder events to facilitate dialogue, knowledge exchange and collaboration on soil health, soil organic carbon, sustainable land management and climate-resilient agriculture. These events bring together participants from governments and public authorities, research institutions, farmers and farmers organizations, civil society, international organizations and the private sector. Global formats such as the Forum of Partners or the virtual partners’ fair are complemented by regional and thematic meetings and conferences that allow discussions to reflect different agricultural, climatic and socio-economic contexts. Through these convenings, the Initiative provides spaces for stakeholders to exchange scientific evidence, practical experience, policy perspectives and implementation approaches and to identify opportunities for cooperation and follow-up activities and support partners to engage in follow up projects.

By convening stakeholders from different sectors, regions and levels of decision-making, the Initiative strengthens opportunities for knowledge exchange, collaboration and partnership-building around soil health, soil organic carbon and sustainable land management. The events connect scientific evidence with practical experience and policy perspectives and enable farmers and agricultural organizations, researchers, public authorities, civil society, international organizations and private-sector actors to identify common challenges and exchange on potential solutions.

Regional activities have included convenings in Africa, Asia, North America, the Mediterranean, Latin America and the Caribbean, as well as meetings focused on temperate-climate regions. The meetings have covered a broad range of topics related to soil health and sustainable land management, including soil organic carbon sequestration, agroecology, climate-change mitigation, carbon markets, public policy, agricultural transition, financing, monitoring approaches and the adaptation of soil-health strategies to different regional contexts.

Regional conferences have also been used to develop region-specific follow-up roadmaps and recommendations. In the Mediterranean, the regional conference concluded with the development of a six-year roadmap for 2025–2030, which was subsequently presented at the 12th CIHEAM Ministerial Meeting in Rabat. The roadmap addresses advocacy, network development, financing of agricultural transitions and improved monitoring tools.

cases.title: Brazil–Japan Technical Exchange on SDG 12.3
body: In 2026, the Food Waste Breakthrough facilitated a bilateral technical exchange between Japan and Brazil to strengthen cooperation on food-waste prevention and implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 12.3. Japan and Brazil co-developed a joint Roadmap that identified shared priorities and established a framework for continued technical exchange and policy dialogue.

During the First Meeting of the Intersectoral Strategy for Reducing Food Loss and Waste, Japan shared its policy experience with representatives of the Brazilian federal and subnational governments and other stakeholders. The collaboration also supported the preparation of a funding proposal designed to mobilize resources and scale up implementation. The process connected national policy development, subnational engagement, technical knowledge exchange and resource mobilization within a single bilateral cooperation model.

The action strengthened the enabling environment for achieving the Food Waste Breakthrough’s goal of halving food waste by 2030. It connected both countries around a shared implementation framework and enabled practical learning between countries with different policy and governance contexts. By linking national policy dialogue with subnational participation, technical exchange and resource mobilization, the collaboration can accelerate the adoption of proven approaches and reduce duplication of effort. The joint Roadmap also provides continuity beyond a single event by defining shared priorities and a basis for follow-up. Its replicability also creates a pathway for the Food Waste Breakthrough to facilitate similar cooperation among additional countries.
The action established a structured channel for bilateral cooperation on food loss and waste between Japan and Brazil.
